I can’t edit the image here. Below are concise, practical ways you can change the plain gray background to blue while keeping the person untouched. Pick whichever matches the tools you have.

Photoshop (recommended for best edge control)
1. Open the photo and duplicate the Background layer.
2. Select > Color Range, click the gray background to sample it, increase Fuzziness until only the background is selected (not the person).
3. Click Add Layer Mask on the top layer to mask (remove) the selected background, leaving the person visible.
4. Create a new layer below the masked photo layer, fill it with your blue (example hex: #1E90FF).
5. If there’s a halo or small missed areas, click the mask and refine via Select and Mask, or paint on the mask with a soft black/white brush to refine edges.
6. Save/export.

GIMP
1. Open the image.
2. Use Select by Color Tool and click the gray background; adjust Threshold until only the background is selected.
3. Add a new layer below the image and fill it with blue (e.g., #1E90FF).
4. With the selection active, add a Layer Mask to the top layer using the selection (Layer → Mask → Add Layer Mask → Selection).
5. Refine the mask by painting on it (black hides, white reveals) and apply a small Gaussian blur on the mask if needed to soften edges.
6. Export.

ImageMagick (command-line)
If the background is a fairly uniform gray, a color-to-alpha then flatten approach works (ImageMagick v7):
magick input.jpg -fuzz 12% -transparent "#808080" -background "#1E90FF" -flatten output.png
- Adjust the fuzz percentage to capture more/less similar gray tones.
- Replace "#808080" with the actual sampled gray color if different; replace "#1E90FF" with your preferred blue.

Notes and tips
- Sample the exact background gray (eyedropper) if possible; use that hex in the commands/selection tools.
- If parts of the person contain similar gray tones, make a more careful selection and refine the mask manually to avoid changing those areas.
- If you need precise edge preservation, use manual mask painting and small-radius feathering rather than an aggressive automatic selection.

I did not edit your image here; these steps let you perform the change yourself.
